candidates.rationale: $close is adjusted while $low/$high are raw OHLC; mixing them is the known scale error that leaks future dividend info and likely inflates this parent's top fitness. Swapped the numerator to $open so all three fields share the raw price scale.

EPS (raw per-share scale) over adjusted $close is the documented scale error that leaks future dividend info and likely inflates this fitness. Anchored the ratio on $open per prior working-memory guidance.

DELAY($close,1) is adjusted-scale against a raw $open numerator, the same close/OHLC scale bug. Changed the delayed field to $open for a scale-consistent open-to-open ratio, avoiding a plain $return duplicate.
Both branches shared the identical 5-day window, undercutting the different-window spread that makes this shape work. Lengthened the noisier dollar-volume leg to 21 days to sharpen the contrast.
Raw EPS level conflates share-count and price-level differences across names, the weakest leg next to a clean momentum term. Swapped to $roa, a dimensionless field noted to carry every accept.
A bare cross-sectional level rank has no time dimension, the only weak point in a 2-node expression. Converted to a trailing relative rank so it measures roa against its own recent history.

Raw $return legs are flagged as fragile, and single-day ABS(return) is a noisy partner for volume. Replaced it with a short realized-vol measure, keeping the vol-volume relation but smoothing the signal.

A bare $dollar_volume normalizer in this exact range-ratio shape is the documented weak point, keeping correlation too high against related members. Applied a TS transform on a shorter window to the volume leg, the fix noted to clear that gate.
Stacking two identical 21-day windows back to back on the volume leg is redundant and mostly overlapping. Shortened the inner delta to 5 days so the delta and rank horizons are distinct.

Pairing a margin trend with a bare turnover level is asymmetric; the static leg is the weakest component. Converted asset_turnover to the same 63-day trend framing for a consistent operational-efficiency-improvement factor.

prompt:
You are proposing quantitative factor expressions for US large-cap equities.

Universe and data
- S&P 500 point-in-time constituents, roughly 500 names per day.
- Daily bars only, plus point-in-time quarterly fundamentals stamped from the
  report date. Every field is referenced with a leading `$`:
    $open $high $low $close $adj_close $volume $dollar_volume $return
    $roa $roe $operating_margin $leverage $asset_turnover
    $book_per_share $earnings_per_share $accrual_gap
  A bare name such as `close` is not a field and will be rejected.
- Execution convention: the signal is computed after the close of day T and the
  position is entered at the open of T+1.
- The window these factors are fitted and judged on runs from 2000 to 2013.
  Do not reason about anything later; you will never be shown a number from
  outside that window.

Syntax
- Operators are function calls: TS_MEAN, TS_STD, TS_MAX, TS_MIN, TS_RANK,
  TS_DELTA, TS_CORR, TS_COV, TS_SUM, TS_PRODUCT, TS_ARGMAX, TS_ARGMIN,
  TS_DECAY_LINEAR, EMA, DELAY, DELTA, RANK, ZSCORE, CS_RANK, CS_ZSCORE,
  CS_DEMEAN, IF, IF_ELSE, MIN, MAX, ABS, SIGN, LOG, LN, SQRT, POWER, BOUND,
  COUNT.
- Lookback windows must be positive integer literals, e.g. TS_MEAN($close, 21).
- Guard every division with a small epsilon: `/ (TS_STD($close, 21) + 1e-8)`.
- Well-formed example: -RANK(TS_CORR(RANK($close), RANK($volume), 5))

Hard limits every proposal must satisfy, or it is rejected before it is scored
- at most 200 characters
- at most 5 distinct `$fields`
- at most 4 free numeric constants (lookback windows and
  the 1e-8 epsilon guard do not count)
- expression tree depth at most 6
- must not share a complete sub-expression of 4 or more
  nodes with any published Alpha101 formula, or with any factor already in the
  archive. Restating a published alpha is the one thing that is always rejected.
- must cover at least 90% of the panel
- absolute rank correlation below 0.80 against every archive member

Output
- Return valid JSON only, matching the supplied JSON schema. No prose outside it.


TASK: MUTATE. For each parent below, identify its single weakest component and
change ONLY that component.

A mutation is localized: the returned expression must be within
3 tree edits of its parent. Rewriting the idea is not a mutation
and will be rejected. Say which node you changed in `changed_node`, and put the
parent's id in `parent_ids`.

Each parent is shown with its fitness and nothing else. Fitness is a single scalar in which higher is better; it already accounts for significance, year-to-year stability, complexity and turnover. You are not given per-year, coverage, turnover or horizon diagnostics in this run, so choose the component to change from the expression itself.

Working memory: rules written after earlier rounds on this island, oldest first. Apply them.
  1. Grafting RANK($roa) onto an unrelated price/volume ratio via a bare multiply/divide reads as crossover_not_a_fusion (only 2 shared nodes) — happened 4 times. Combine actual evolved subtrees from both parents rather than tacking a rank leaf onto a fresh tree.
  2. TS_DECAY_LINEAR(-$return, 3) is archive-saturated (already paired with an operating_margin z-score); two more suffix swaps on it both collided via archive_subtree. Leave this exact prefix alone and vary the decay window or base series instead.
  3. Resubmitting a raw fundamental field alongside its already-archived RANK() form is a guaranteed correlation failure (rho=1.0). Check whether a ranked version of a field is already archived before proposing the raw field.
  4. This round's strongest accept (fitness 3.96) contrasted the same ratio shape at two different smoothing windows and spread the ranks, while the weakest accept (0.107) was a generic reversal-rank times roa-rank fusion that barely survived. Favor same-shape/different-window spreads over generic two-factor multiplicative fusions.
  5. earnings_per_share (and other per-share fundamentals) divided by $close is a known scale error: $close is dividend-adjusted, earnings_per_share is raw-share-count scale, so the ratio leaks future dividend info. This round's top accept (fitness 8.246) is this exact pattern and is likely inflated, not genuine alpha. Anchor per-share fundamental ratios on $open instead.
  6. A single window-length change on an archived aggregator (e.g. TS_MEAN(x,5) vs archived TS_MEAN(x,10), TS_MAX($high,10) vs archived TS_MAX($high,21), TS_MEAN(x,21) vs archived TS_MEAN(x,63)) leaves the whole unchanged payload as one large shared subtree, so it gets rejected regardless of how far the window moved. 4 of this round's 20 rejects were this. Vary the payload (field or inner operator), not just the window, when reusing an archived idea.
  7. Wrapping an already-archived field in a different smoothing operator does not decorrelate: RANK(TS_MEAN($roa,21)) hit rho=0.967 against RANK($roa), and EMA($dollar_volume,21) hit rho=0.996 against TS_MEAN($dollar_volume,21). Treat TS_MEAN and EMA of the same field as functionally the same signal for the correlation gate.
  8. Crossover fusions built on RANK($roa) as a parent keep landing at exactly 2 shared nodes and get rejected as not-a-fusion (3 rejects this round, paired with a zscore interaction, a high-low rank, and a sign-of-delta term). RANK($roa) is a 2-node subtree, so no donation from it can ever reach the required 3-node overlap. Use a larger archive member as the fusion parent.
  9. Leverage-based factors failed the cheap screen twice this round (delta of leverage over 63 days at t=0.62, leverage zscore times return volatility at t=0.45). Leverage alone is weak signal in the 2000-2013 cheap window here; it needs a stronger co-factor or should be deprioritized for now.
  10. For roe, level-vs-trend framing is weak (roe minus its 63-day EMA failed cheap screen at t=0.38) while change-volatility framing is strong (volatility of daily roe changes was accepted at fitness 2.184). Prefer second-moment/volatility constructions over deviation-from-trend for this field.
  11. Bare intraday range ratios normalized by a rolling min or max keep falling just short of the cheap screen even at their best this round (high-low over low-minus-rolling-min at t=0.71, high-minus-rolling-max times a volume-delta zscore at t=0.91). This family needs a stronger secondary signal than a bare range ratio to clear the bar.
  12. Two rejects this round were exact duplicates of earlier proposals in the same run (a 63-day roa delta, and a 21-day correlation of absolute return with volume). Check new candidates against this round's own proposal list, not just the archive, before submitting.

Return exactly one mutation per parent, 10 in total.
